title: Functions, References, Classes, and RAII
summary: Design function contracts and small classes using references, const correctness, constructors, private state, invariants, and automatic resource lifetime.
learningObjectives: Explain and apply Functions, References, Classes, and RAII
Compile and test behavior with observable evidence
prerequisiteConcepts: Ability to create and save a text file

sections.heading: Core model
sections.content: Arguments are passed by value unless a reference type is declared. Use `const T&` for read-only access to a potentially expensive object and `T&` for deliberate caller-visible mutation. Return values are usually clear and efficiently optimized. A class should keep fields private and establish invariants in its constructor. RAII ties resource lifetime to object lifetime: containers, strings, file streams, and smart pointers release resources through destructors. Prefer these owners over manual `new` and `delete`. Mark member functions `const` when they do not modify observable state.
